proof_attempt_summary: Derived universal-constant complete-block raw/cube minimax bounds, finite rational rate evaluation, arbitrary-sequence consistency criteria, additive/full-order boundaries and one growing-order envelope separation. Math and rubric reviews passed without findings; independent MAIN validity sustained the typed incremental tier below the fixed field floor (5.8 < 7.4). tldr: Raw coefficient mass and bounded outcomes impose different growing-order precision constraints on the same total treatment effect. In a single fair Bernoulli experiment on public complete interference blocks, a finite coefficient program characterizes raw-class minimax mean squared error with constants uniform in block count, degree and interaction order. The bounded-cube Fourier benchmark gives the second envelope. Explicit critical scales characterize consistency along arbitrary joint sequences, additive and full-order boundaries recover familiar rates, and a growing-order sequence separates the envelopes. An open question asks whether public odd-order cutoff scores capture the entire raw frontier or whether the general bias-aware weights are essential.
gap: Fixed-order precision guarantees can hide an interaction-order dependence in the legal lower signal. The minimum-energy Fourier representer has bounded cube norm but can have exponentially growing raw coefficient mass.
fill: The raw coefficient Gram program, total attaining weights, and budget-legal full-record converse give a universal frontier. Arithmetic critical scales and an evaluated separating sequence make its consequences visible to sample-size and complexity planning.
